parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with appointments, so the module holds together as one concern. VisitNotesService breaks the boundary, though. It is given a PrismaService through its constructor and uses it in write(). But notesFor() builds its own client with `new PrismaClient()` from @prisma/client and queries visitNote.findMany on it. That skips the module's own injected persistence port and goes to the ORM directly. The candidate flags about direct ORM/DB access at line 21 are confirmed. The domain-does-io flags at lines 14-16 and 22 point at the same direct Prisma access. SchedulingService only reaches persistence through its injected DAOs and uses the domain entities consistently. It repeats the Appointment row-to-entity mapping in book() and cancel(), but that is mapping code, not a duplicated rule or invariant, so I don't count it as a violation.
